key_insight: This paper explores how far implicit neural representations (INRs) can be pushed for brain MRI segmentation, showing that they can deliver strong cross-domain performance with far fewer parameters than conventional models. The key takeaway is that lightweight INR-based segmentation can be both efficient and robust under distribution shifts.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of performing accurate biomedical image segmentation when annotations are limited, model memory is constrained, and data comes from different sites or domains with distribution shifts.
method: Uses implicit neural representations (INRs) as a parameter-efficient alternative to standard segmentation networks.
Studies scaling behavior and the mechanisms behind INR-based segmentation performance.
Evaluates cross-domain generalization for brain MRI segmentation under site/domain shifts.
impact: This matters because it points to a practical path for deploying segmentation models in real clinical settings where memory, data, and generalization are major constraints. For practitioners, it suggests a compact model class that may be easier to train, deploy, and transfer across institutions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing MRI input -> INR model -> segmentation mask output
Comparison bar chart of parameter count vs. segmentation accuracy against conventional methods
Cross-site/domain shift illustration showing training site and target site MRI scans
Icon set for efficiency, robustness, and medical deployment
paper_title: How Far Can INRs Go? Cross-Domain Parameter-efficient INR-Based Semantic Segmentation for Brain MRI
paper_authors: Ziyao Shang, Pouya Sadeghi, Letian Jiang, Alexander Wong, Sirisha Rambhatla
